max_tire.note: GXOR's limit with no modification at all; 255/75R17 also fits with no rubbing. One owner reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse on 265/70.
Fits without a lift only with a body mount chop and the fender liner reshaped with a heat gun (and maybe a knife).
The usual route to 33s. Expect some fender-liner trimming; owners on 285/70R17 with about 2.5–3 in of lift still cut a little liner.
One GXOR database entry, on 18x9 −12 wheels, with the body mounts cut back.

items.title: Side curtain airbag control module
items.summary: The airbag control module may be misprogrammed and fire the side curtain-shield airbags without a crash. Dealers replace the module.

items.title: Second-row seat latch (Lexus Link trucks)
items.summary: On trucks with the Lexus Link case, one latch on the larger second-row seat section may not lock. Dealers trim the case panels.

items.title: Incorrect GVWR on certification label
items.summary: The label printed 6,100 lb instead of the correct 6,000 lb GVWR. Dealers supply a corrected, VIN-specific label.

items.title: Load and GVWR labels on accessorized trucks
items.summary: Accessories fitted at vehicle processing centers could push some trucks over the labelled GVWR. Dealers replace the labels.

tsbs.title: Cracked, sticky or melting dashboard
tsbs.summary: Warranty Enhancement Program covering instrument-panel damage from heat and humidity on 2003–2008 GX 470s.

timeline.change: Launch at the 2002 Detroit show, on sale November 2002. 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 at 235 hp, five-speed automatic, rear air suspension. Rated to tow 5,000 lb.
Sealed transmission (no dipstick), TPMS, roll-sensing curtain airbags and an optional backup camera. A mid-year hitch upgrade raised towing to 6,500 lb, and KDSS became optional late in the year.
VVT-i lifts output to 270 hp with ULEV II certification. Bluetooth and a new Sport model with KDSS standard.
Same engine, restated at 263 hp under revised SAE testing. Lexus Link telematics offered.
New-generation navigation, auxiliary input jack and a larger optional rear-seat screen.
Facelift: dark metallic grille, liquid-graphite wheels, more chrome and revised turn signals.
Final year. Only 6,235 GXs were sold in calendar 2009 before the GX 460 took over.

identify.intro: Every US GX 470 is a Tahara-built Land Cruiser Prado 120 underneath, so the questions are about options, not authenticity: KDSS, the hitch rating and whether the air suspension is still there.

items.head: VIN
items.body: US trucks start JTJBT20X. NHTSA's vPIC decoder reads the series as UZJ120L, the engine as the 2UZ-FE and the plant as Tahara, Japan. The 10th character is the model year (3 = 2003 through 9 = 2009).

items.head: KDSS
items.body: Optional from late in the 2004 model year and standard on the 2005-on Sport. Look for a momentary KDSS light at key-on and the noticeably large front sway bar.

items.head: Hitch rating
items.body: 2003 trucks are rated for 5,000 lb. The stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch arrived during the 2004 model year with a 6,500 lb rating, so check what's actually bolted on.

items.head: Sport model
items.body: From 2005: KDSS, smoked headlamp bezels, extra chrome trim and black birdseye maple wood.

items.head: Facelift trucks
items.body: 2008–2009 trucks have the dark metallic grille and liquid-graphite wheels.

items.head: Rear suspension
items.body: Rear air suspension shares its layout with the air-sprung 4th-gen 4Runner. Many trucks have been converted to coils, which is worth knowing before you look for the height-control switch.

values.intro: The GX 470 has become the default budget overlander, and clean, low-mile trucks now sell for more than many GX 460s.
values.note: Based on 115 Bring a Trailer GX 470 sales from January 2025 to October 2026, which ranged from $4,400 to $41,750 with a median of $20,000. The top sales were trucks with under 40,000 miles.
